title: Ash Lake
snippet:
Ash Lake -  Dark Souls - location - description 
 description : Ash Lake is an optional area accessed by successfully reaching the bottom of The Great Hollow, through a tunnel past the Mushroom enemies. It is a wide, open space with seemingly endless views of Archtrees amidst deep, dark blue waters and below a sky of dense clouds. A large stretch of sand connects two Archtrees, and the shores abruptly end, leading to a watery grave.

The Stone Dragon is a passive and invulnerable entity that serves as initiator to the Path of the Dragon covenant.

title: Ash Lake
snippet:
Ash Lake -  Dark Souls - location - lead 
 lead : **Ash Lake** is a location in *Dark Souls*.

title: Ash Lake
snippet:
Ash Lake -  Dark Souls - location - notes 
 notes : If one continues through Ash Lake without defeating the Hydra, it will attempt to follow the player. Once the player passes the area where the Giant Clams are, the Hydra will jump out of the water and fly across the beach to the other side to continue to pursue the player. It will then follow all the way to the Archtree near the end of the area. This makes confrontation with the Hydra almost completely unavoidable.
**It's possible to avoid the Hydra by wearing the Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring while staying near the opposite shore of the beach. Doing so will allow the player to advance outside of the Hydra's aggro range and continue undisturbed all the way to the Stone Dragon.

title: Basilisk
snippet:
Basilisk -  Dark Souls - enemy - critical 
 critical : Hitting any part of a basilisk's face will deal increased damage. Because the face is the point that gets targeted when locking onto the basilisk, using thrust attacks will work exceedingly well against basilisks, as each strike will almost guarantee this bonus damage.

title: Basilisk
snippet:
Basilisk -  Dark Souls - enemy - melee 
 melee : Basilisks have no melee attacks whatsoever. Combined with relatively low health, they can be quickly dealt with. However getting too close risks exposure to Curse and is ill-advised if they are in any significant numbers, or the player has low Curse resistance.

Considering their only means of offense are their Curse attacks, the player could equip a shield with high Curse block in order to take basilisks down more easily. Spears and Thrusting Swords are excellent for this strategy, as they can strike from behind shields.

title: Basilisk
snippet:
Basilisk -  Dark Souls - enemy - general_information 
 general_information : The basilisk can only cause curse status; they cause no other effects or any direct damage in any form unless they jump directly on the player.

The basilisks in the Depths guard the Ring of the Evil Eye.

title: Basilisk
snippet:
Basilisk -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Basilisks have low health and no poise, making them easy to kill with almost any attack. Their most dangerous move is the leaping curse breath attack, due to its low wind-up, while their standing curse breath is far more telegraphed and easily interrupted. With sufficient curse resistance and rapid offense even groups of basilisks won't prove too challenging as long as the player is mindful of the clouds.

Basilisks are deaf, meaning they struggle to detect the player unless they see or touch them. Even if they do detect the player, they are slow to turn around, often favoring simply running away before turning around, meaning that they struggle to react to the player getting behind them.

title: Basilisk
snippet:
Basilisk -  Dark Souls - enemy - description 
 description : Basilisks are slender, scrawny lizards. Upon seeing the player, it will frantically scramble or leap into position and exhale a grey mist that will quickly overwhelm the player with the Curse status, causing immediate death.

The bulbous appendages that appear on the basilisk are not its actual eyes. The basilisk's true eyes are the small yellow beads that appear right over its mouth.

title: Basilisk
snippet:

title: Basilisk

title: Basilisk
snippet:
Basilisk -  Dark Souls - enemy - ranged 
 ranged : Basilisks stagger from just about any hit, and can easily be pelted with arrows without them being able to execute a single attack. This gives the added bonus of allowing players to pull one or two basilisks at a time, rather than have the entire swarm of seven or so rushing after them.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - quelaag_s_domain_bell 
 quelaag_s_domain_bell : The other Bell is significantly harder to reach. The Chosen Undead must first head downward and find their way into Blighttown, a multileveled and dangerous labyrinth. At the very bottom of Blighttown, the player will traverse a poison swamp leading to a half-demon's lair known as Quelaag's Domain. It is here that the player must defeat Chaos Witch Quelaag in order to progress to the Bell of Awakening.

Upon ringing the second Bell, a short cutscene plays showing the gatekeeper Giant hearing the call and pulling the chains to lift up the portcullis, bearing passage to Sen's Fortress. It is at this point that Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine, and instructs the player that his new task is to secure the Lordvessel, proving that the player is in fact, the Chosen Undead.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bells of Awakening** are a storyline concept, as well as two locations, in *Dark Souls*.

They are the first destinations hinted at for the Chosen Undead after they have escaped the Undead Asylum into Lordran. The two Bells are part of a prophecy devised by the Gods of Anor Londo to help bring about an Undead to link the First Flame. The two Bells are respectively located past the Bell Gargoyles atop the Undead Parish, and past Queelag past the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown. Both Bells must be rung by activating levers near them to progress, opening the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - plot 
 plot : The Bells of Awakening are hinted at being the first destination of the Chosen Undead and, when rung, the fate of the undead shall be known. Upon arriving in Firelink Shrine, the Crestfallen Warrior informs the player that there are, in fact, two Bells of Awakening. One up above and one far below. This is essentially all the instruction and plot that is revealed upon arrival in Lordran.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Ringing the bell in Quelaag's Domain first will have no different effect than if the player rang the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] first. Although this will cause Lautrec's questline to progress, leading to the death of Anastacia.
The Bells of Awakening were used to awaken Kingseeker Frampt and open the way to Sen's Fortress.

title: Bells of Awakening

Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - undead_church_bell 
 undead_church_bell : One of the Bells is located in the Undead Parish, up above from Firelink Shrine. After dispatching the Bell Gargoyles, the Chosen Undead is able to climb to the top of the Church Belltower and ring the Bell of Awakening.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - notes 
 notes : In the Prepare to Die Edition, online players in the vicinity of the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] were able to hear the bell being rung from other player worlds. This wasn’t the case for the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Bell in Quelaag’s Domain].
In the remastered version of the game, online players are now able to hear either the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Parish_bell.jpg Undead Parish Bell] or the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Quelaag’s domain Bell] being rung from other player worlds while exploring one area or the other . (as the [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/File:Quelaag_bell.jpg Quelaag’s Bell] toll was specifically added in the remaster)

title: Blighttown
snippet:
Blighttown -  Dark Souls - location - strategies 
 strategies : In general, high poison resistance will serve the player greatly while navigating both the upper and lower parts; it buys more time while navigating the poison swamp before being poisoned and gives a better chance of avoiding becoming toxic from blowdarts.
Care should be taken when using weapons with attacks that move the player, such as curved swords, as the additional movement may lead to unintended falls.
There are multiple bridges in the upper area that will shift and move while the player walks on them. Caution should be used while on these.
The Rusted Iron Ring will negate the slowing effect of the poison sludge, allowing players to traverse the area considerably faster.
**Standard rolls are not affected by the slowing effect and can be used to speed up travel through the swamp. However, the Dark Wood Grain Ring's special roll can only be used in slowing terrain if the Rusted Iron Ring is also worn.

title: Blighttown
snippet:
Blighttown -  Dark Souls - location - description 
 description : Blighttown is a rather treacherous area with a high degree of verticality. It can be accessed through either the Depths through defeating the Gaping Dragon and acquiring the Blighttown Key, or the Valley of Drakes by navigating through Darkroot Basin from the Undead Parish.

The upper parts consist of interconnecting bridges and scaffolding, with plenty of places to fall to one's death if not careful. The bottom portion of the area is a poisonous swamp that will slow the player's movements.

Many enemies in the area can inflict poison, while Blowdart Snipers are able to deal Toxic from a great distance.

title: Blowdart Sniper
snippet: Other than the darts, they have no other way of attacking the player other than a weak shove at close range. Assuming that there isn't more than one sniper attacking at once, running past them can work if the player is fast enough.

title: Blowdart Sniper
snippet:
Blowdart Sniper -  Dark Souls - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : A minimum of 81 poison resistance is required to avoid becoming toxic in one shot from a blowdart without blocking.
Because they appear in dark, secluded areas, can detect the player from long distances, and start shooting continuously with high precision once they've detected the player, the snipers may intoxicate a player before they even know where the shots are coming from. Therefore, it is viable to employ some form of stealth such as the Ring of Fog to greatly reduce the distance at which a sniper becomes hostile.
A rather effective, though unsavory, way of countering them is to intoxicate yourself using a few Dung Pies dropped from the Infested Barbarians throughout upper Blighttown. The effect is unstackable and only deals 7 HP/sec in damage as opposed to 14 HP/sec from the snipers.

Their darts inflict an extremely high amount of Toxic buildup. Their toxin is the most dangerous in the game, as although it is the briefest one in duration it also deals the most amount of damage per second.

 characteristics : The Falchion has the same scaling, moveset, attack speed, and stamina consumption as the Scimitar, but has higher base damage. In terms of damage output, the Falchion loses to the Painting Guardian Sword at higher levels; however, it possesses a slightly longer reach.

The Falchion is one of lowest stamina-consuming weapons in the game, meaning that in conjunction with its fast attacks, the Falchion is capable of quickly dispatching enemies.

title: Smouldering Lake
snippet: An unconfirmed, yet possible, theory is that the Smouldering Lake is another section of the Ash Lake from *Dark Souls*. This theory is supported by the presence of massive trees, resembling the archtrees that the ancient dragons once lived in and that the witches of Izalith burned with their pyromancy. It is also supported by the close proximity the Ash Lake had to the Demon Ruins as well. Looking from a top-down view from Blighttown, one could see that the entrance to the Demon Ruins was right across from the entrance to the Ash Lake; and as both were beneath, then it would seem reasonable that the two areas were in close proximity to each other.

title: The Gutter
snippet: The level is filled with hollows, who may mob and ambush unsuspecting players who venture forth without a source of light and do not keep an eye on their surroundings. While not very threatening individually, the level's vertical design and lack of light allows them to surprise players at inopportune moments. Care should be taken while navigating the Gutter so as to avoid being overwhelmed or knocked into the abyss.

snippet:

 location : Grandahl is found in three separate shrines throughout Drangleic. These shrines are often in hidden places and they all need to be found to activate Grandahl's services as the Pilgrims of Dark Covenant leader. These places are often accessed via dropping, and are located in the Black Gulch, Shaded Woods, and Drangleic Castle.
To open The Black Gulch entrance, the player will need the Forgotten Key gained from killing two Elite Giants in a cave located underneath the door's platform.
The Shaded Woods access point is located to the right of the path that leads up to the Scorpioness Najka fight. The player will find a grassy patch to the right and fall through the boards in the ground, finding the shrine.

title: Player versus Player
snippet: Black Phantoms may only invade players who have not yet cleared an area's boss. Thus, it is impossible to invade in some places that do not have bosses, such as the Firelink Shrine and Ash Lake.

title: Hydra
snippet:
Hydra -  Dark Souls - enemy - ash_lake 
 ash_lake : The Ash Lake Hydra rests near the edge of a sandbar entering the lake. Some distance from the Hydra, a large log lies on top of a ridge of the sandbar. Sheltering behind this log will attract long range attacks from the Hydra, which will be blocked completely by the log. It is possible to shelter behind the log and attack the Hydra safely with a bow; the Hawk Ring and Dragonslayer Greatbow are recommended. When the Hydra is already at very low health, the Symbol of Avarice and Covetous Silver Serpent Ring can be equipped to increase the number of souls gained when the Hydra dies. Equipping the Symbol of Avarice will mean shooting blind, but the Hydra is so large that it is easy to continue hitting its body (it is not necessary or advisable to aim for the heads), for the last few shots required to kill it.

title: Skeleton Boulder
snippet:
The hooded skeleton controlling this boulder can be found overlooking on the second floor, although it will be heavily guarded by three Skeleton Swordsmen. To reach this area, the player can take the second doorway on the left. However, a safer route can be found by hitting an illusory wall to the left of this archway, uncovering another path that will provide a more strategic approach.

Once this boulder breaks apart, it will drop a Dark Gem and also release a Lesser Crab.

title: Horace the Hushed
snippet: Horace can be seen standing at the bottom of the large chasm below the hanging bridge that leads to High Lord Wolnir. The access to this location can be found via climbing down the bridge after destroying it to access Smouldering Lake, and then navigating a long tunnel on the right side upon entering the lake proper. Upon approach, however, Horace will attack the player (presumably due to hollowing), leaving no other option than to fight back. He wields a regular Halberd, and will use its Charge skill quite often to close the distance.

title: Pilgrims of Dark
snippet:
Pilgrims of Dark -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Players must talk to Darkdiver Grandahl in three separate locations:
#Shaded Woods: From the Shaded Ruins bonfire, advance forward until an open area is reached. Start walking right and past the two towers that lead to Scorpioness Najka. There will be a boarded up hole in the nearby grassy area by the cliff, which will let the player drop down to Grandahl. To break it, the player must simply walk over it.
#Black Gulch: Dropping down from the cliff near the two Razorback Nightcrawlers will land the player on a ledge with a locked door. To obtain the key for it, drop down two more times into an enclave that houses two Elite Giants; killing them will grant the Forgotten Key, along with a Soul of a Giant.

title: High Wall of Lothric
snippet:
This is the first level where a crossbow can be obtained; while crossbow-wielding hollows appeared in the previous level, they do not drop the weapon.
After Vordt is slain, it is possible to walk out to the very edge of the cliff and see all but three areas in the base game that can be explored: the Undead Settlement, the Cathedral of the Deep, the Road of Sacrifices and the adjacent Farron Keep and swamp, Irithyll of the Boreal Valley and Anor Londo, and Archdragon Peak. The areas that cannot be seen are underground areas: Irithyll Dungeon and connected Profaned Capital, and the Catacombs of Carthus. One other, unknown, location is seen far off into the mountains, between the Settlement and the Cathedral: the size of a village or small town, with trees and buildings clearly seen.

title: Smouldering Lake
snippet:
Inside the Demon Ruins reside Smouldering Ghrus, Demon Clerics, Demon Statues, Hound Rats and Giant Hound Rats, Basilisks, and two Black Knights. To reach the upper reaches of the lake, a long, winding route through the ruins must be taken, with a great number of these enemies along the way.

In the deepest part of the ruins, above a pool of deadly lava, there is a ladder leading up to the high ledges above the lake, guarded by a Black Knight. Below, Knight Slayer Tsorig can be found. Once emerging on the ledge, a few ballista bolts must be avoided, but the rock formations will prevent most of them from reaching below. A few Skeletons, Skeleton Wheels and Skeleton Swordsmen patrol this area. Past them, the ballista is spinning its gears and can be deactivated with a lever, making the lower area of the lake substantially safer to traverse. A series of ledges against the wall can be dropped down to reach the bottom quickly.

title: Sieglinde of Catarina
snippet: **Other details suggest that, in the final version of the game, Sieglinde is intended to be Undead. The player can steal 10 Humanity from Sieglinde with the Dark Hand, and only an Undead would have reason to hold more than a single Humanity. Her continued affection for Siegmeyer suggests that Catarina may not hate Undead as much as other regions. Also, it is implausible that an ordinary Human could traverse the Great Hollow and reach the bottom of Ash Lake without being killed.

title: Crest Shield
snippet:
Crest Shield -  Dark Souls - shield - characteristics 
 characteristics : What sets the Crest Shield apart from other medium shields is its massive 80% magic reduction. This makes the Crest Shield a powerful asset when facing magic-dealing enemies. When used in conjunction with miracles such as Great Magic Barrier, the player can become virtually immune to magic damage.

The Crest Shield has medium deflection and a normal parry speed.

title: Engraved Gauntlets
snippet:
Engraved Gauntlets -  Dark Souls II - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : At first glance, the Engraved Gauntlets seem to be very poor stat-wise, as they offer little physical and elemental resistances; however, they makes up for it by having the highest Curse and Petrification resistances in the game for hand armor, and by having a unique effect of a 5% chance for normal hits to deal damage equal to a critical attack. When this effect is triggered, the gauntlets cause an explosion, releasing what seems to be ash around the player.

title: Smouldering Lake
snippet:
On the highest ledge above the Smouldering Lake, a colossal triple ballista fires giant bolts at anyone trying to cross the lake. It is fully automated and the Giant Slaves that maintained it are long dead. It represents a significant threat; however, it can be used to one's advantage by getting a bolt to hit the unstable floor in the middle of the lake, opening an entrance to the Old King's Antechamber. Additionally, at the far wall left of the ballista is a crumbling wall which hides the Speckled Stoneplate Ring, and demolishing the wall with a bolt allows access to it.

Another entrance to the Demon Ruins lies straight ahead from the entrance to the lake, near the chamber of the Old Demon King. However, burrowed into the ground nearby is a Carthus Sand Worm, which will shoot up when someone comes nearby. As bolts from the ballista can also reach this area, it is an extremely dangerous route to take.

title: Mushroom People
snippet:
This is not the only place where they dwell, however, as they inhabit the hollowed out insides of a great tree situated at the foot of Blighttown. They are also found inside nearby trees in the Ash Lake, situated at the roots of the Great Hollow. This might suggest they originated from inside these imposing descendants of the Archtrees in a much older age.

They appear to be the source of Gold Pine Resin, as it is believed to be fungal in nature and the Mushroom People drop the substance upon death.

snippet:
Siegmeyer of Catarina -  Dark Souls - character - removed_content 
 removed_content : From text dumps, Siegmeyer was supposed to encounter Basilisks, probably in the Depths or in The Great Hollow. The player can choose to help him there in a similar fashion to his other encounters. Siegmeyer was also aware that his journey to Ash Lake would be his last; he also has removed dialogue with the player after meeting with.

This video shows Siegmeyer's entire dialogue including cut content dialogue. [https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=PBKDEQZSAsk]

title: Giant Clam
snippet:
Giant Clam -  Dark Souls - enemy - notes 
 notes : Giant Clams are an easy source of Twinkling Titanite, an otherwise expensive upgrade material. They can be farmed in Ash Lake and the Crystal Cave, where they can be respawned repeatedly.
Shooting an arrow into a Giant Clam's mouth will briefly stun it.
When encountering Seath the Scaleless for the first time, in the Crystal Cave, the fog wall is not present. This allows the clams the chance to enter the room that houses the boss fight, if the player tries to run past them. Seath's attacks can harm them, but they will still only attack the player, making the fight a fair bit more challenging.

title: Ashen Estus Flask
snippet:
Ashen Estus Flask -  Dark Souls III - item - overview 
 overview : Drinking from the Ashen Estus Flask restores FP, much like how the normal Estus Flask restores HP. Resting at a bonfire will refill it to maximum charges.

The total number of shared charges between the normal Estus Flask and Ashen Estus Flask can be increased by bringing Estus Shards to Blacksmith Andre, and the potency of each charge increased by burning an Undead Bone Shard at Firelink Shrine's bonfire. The number of total charges between the two flasks can reach a maximum of 15, while the potency of the flasks can reach a maximum of +10. The player can also talk to Blacksmith Andre to allot their Estus charges between the two flasks.

The potency of each charge of the Ashen Estus Flask can be increased by 20% by equipping the Ashen Estus Ring.

title: Great Crab
snippet:
If the player befriended the giant archer in the Undead Settlement, he will aid in killing the Great Crab in the Farron Keep, which guards the Crown of Dusk among other items.

If the player wants to fight those encountered in the Smouldering Lake, it's recommended to make a detour through the Demon Ruins first and turn off the ballista. A series of ledges can be found near it, which the player can drop onto to head back to the lake and near from where the Great Crabs are.

Gold Pine Resin -  Dark Souls - item - availability 
 availability : ×3 in a chest on a ledge accessible only with the Master Key (starting gift, or purchased off Domhnall of Zena) or the Residence Key (purchased off the Undead Male Merchant) in the Undead Burg.
Dropped by Mushroom Parents in the Darkroot Garden and The Great Hollow at an 80% drop rate for 1 & a 20% for 2
Dropped by Mushroom Children in the Darkroot Garden and The Great Hollow at a 5% drop rate
Domhnall of Zena sells 3 per playthrough
Elizabeth sells 5 per playthrough

title: Starting Gifts
snippet:
Starting Gifts -  Dark Souls - item - black_firebomb 
 black_firebomb : Black Firebomb ×10. Throwable item that creates a powerful blaze, inflicting Fire Damage to those near the impact. They can be used to easily defeat the Asylum Demon when first encountered and therefore is a relatively easy way to obtain the Demon's Great Hammer on the first playthrough.

title: Zweihander
snippet:
Contrary to popular belief, Zweihander is NOT a "Strength Weapon" but is a "Quality" Scaling weapon meaning it scales near equally off Strength and Dexterity and will be at its full potential at the relevant stat softcaps.

The overhead swing also has the advantage of a high vertical reach. This makes it a very good weapon to use to cut Dragon tails: most other Ultra Greatswords will require a running attack to swing upwards, and Great Hammers don't reach quite as high. The overhead swing also makes the player dodge certain attacks that reach horizontally.

The Zweihander can be a very strong weapon early in the game due to its close proximity to the starting area and relatively low stat requirement of 16 Strength to two-hand the weapon. Even un-upgraded, its base damage and staggering abilities are formidable for the Undead Burg area.

title: Claymore (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Claymore (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Like in the previous games, the Claymore is a reliable and versatile weapon with great damage output. It's balanced scaling between Strength and Dexterity makes it a great candidate for Refined infusion, and it can be buffed with spells and items. This, coupled with its adaptable moveset and early accessibility, makes the Claymore a promising weapon for any melee build.

The Claymore is also one of the longest Greatswords in the game, giving it a better reach than most swords of its class. This allows certain character builds to perform multiple attacks and roll away with near-impunity, particularly during boss fights. Its Weapon Arts is particularly effective against enemies with weapons no longer than a Spear as it makes full use of the sword's length. As with its previous incarnations, the Claymore remains exceptional at stun-locking enemies with low poise.

Cemetery of Ash

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - drops 
 drops : Gwyn's armor, the Set of the Great Lord, can be purchased from Domhnall of Zena during the next playthrough.

title: Hellkite Drake
snippet:
In order to progress into the Undead Parish, the player has two options:

Run across the bridge hugging the right hand side, go down the stairs to the right and kick down the ladder that leads to the Undead Burg Bonfire. Go back up to the bridge and wait in the safe pockets that are on either side of the bridge. Watch the Hellkite Drake and wait a moment. The Drake will land on the bridge and players can run right past it to Sunlight Altar Bonfire located in the room directly below where the Drake perches.
There is a route underneath the bridge, close to the shortcut to the Undead Burg bonfire. It is guarded by two Hollow Soldiers and several Undead Rats. This route has no rest points until one reaches the bonfire close to Andre of Astora, so it is more punishing should the player die en route to their objective.

title: Crystal Cave
snippet:
Crystal Cave -  Dark Souls - location - description 
 description : This area is characterized by walkways of which some are invisible. Snowflakes falling from the ceiling and orange guidance signs etched from other worlds can guide the player on these walkways. The player can also shoot arrows at the air, or drop Prism Stones to see if they stick. The enemies may prove to be an annoyance when on narrow crystal walkways. This makes it easy for the player to fall off with or without being hit.

Crystal Cave is a good location for farming Twinkling Titanite because it's a common drop from Giant Clams, especially with raised Item Discovery. Killing Seath first to unlock the bonfire in the boss area just next to the cave with a group of Giant Clams makes for easy farming.

title: Bonfire (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
***Dragon-Kin Mausoleum**
:As this bonfire's name implies, it is located inside the big mausoleum erected behind from where the Ancient Wyvern makes its last stand. To reach it, the player must defeat the wyvern, either in close combat or by killing it in one hit with a plunging attack at the end of a long gauntlet of enemies. Either way, the player will be automatically teleported to the bonfire once the boss has been defeated.

***Great Belfry**
:This bonfire is located far into the level, after traveling through a few long, open side paths of the sanctuary. At one point, the player will reach a small corner room where a Man Serpent Summoner will continuously summon the Rapier Champion. The bonfire is located on the next corner room, past the great belfry that gives access to the Nameless King boss fight.

title: Brightstone Cove Tseldora
snippet:
Brightstone Cove Tseldora -  Dark Souls II - location - notes 
 notes : The lower bonfire provides a route to the second section of the area, as you reach the second section you drop down into a room with a skeleton corpse, an item and a large sand mound covering most of the room. This mound can be used to jump off and land back onto the path (first section). This will save the use of 10+ homeward bones when soul farming.

title: Friede's Great Scythe
snippet: These advantages do not come without drawbacks, however. In order to wield the weapon, players must first invest a non-negligible amount of levels in Faith, which makes the weapon more difficult to build for. Additionally, despite what is listed in the weapon's information, with its normal moveset it cannot inflict Magic damage at all. As such, in regular situations this reaper is little different from the Pontiff Knight Great Scythe.

title: Siegmeyer of Catarina
snippet: If Siegmeyer jumps down and retains more than 50% of his health by the end of the encounter, he can then be found in Ash Lake. With no more pride and resolve, Siegmeyer had nothing, and when Undead lose everything, they turn Hollow. He then proceeds to attack his daughter, Sieglinde of Catarina, who defeats him. The player arrives too late to save him and witnesses Sieglinde crying over his broken corpse, then gives the player a Titanite Slab.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - notes 
 notes : It is possible to reach and kill the Four Kings by killing Ingward, even if the player hasn't acquired the Lordvessel yet.
The bonfire that appears *will* allow warping to escape the Abyss, even without the Lordvessel.
**This can be used as a shortcut for far away locations, such as Anor Londo, Tomb of the Giants or Ash Lake. If the player avoids resting at other bonfires, the Abyss can be used as a "home base", warping to locations in Lordran, and returning via Homeward Bone.
Although it appears to be a black void of nothingness, the "ground" of the abyss actually floats a few meters above an unseen cobblestone floor. This can be observed by using a light source, such as the Skull Lantern or Sunlight Maggot.
Items that require hitting a surface to activate, such as Prism Stones and Carvings, will not work in the Abyss as they simply fall through the "floor".

title: Sen's Fortress
snippet:
The rolling ball trap is a tricky situation to contend with: initially, when a player first reaches it, it appears as though the direction of the balls can be manually controlled via the central mechanism, and while this is indeed true, the mechanism will actually reset itself should the player move far enough away. It will generally not reset while the player is on a potentially hazardous ball ramp / grove, but *can* reset if the player goes from one grove to the other, and will seemingly do so as if aiming for the player.
** Interacting with this ball trap mechanism is necessary to reach certain optional sections of the fortress. Covetous Gold Serpent Ring can only accessed by filling the zig-zagging stair route with several balls, and Big Hat Logan's imprisonment area can be found by rolling a ball down the central ramp (the one facing the fortress' entrance).

title: Smouldering Lake
snippet:
Smouldering Lake -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : The Smouldering Lake is a shallow lake that lies deep underground. Enormous trees that smoulder with embers grow up to the ceiling and their roots reach far into the chambers below the lake. It has been known to be the remains of the once molten Lost Izalith, or an area adjacent to the lost city. After many years, the lava had subsided significantly; the evidence to this being the presence of the demon corpses that litter the ground in the Demon Ruins, which in *Dark Souls* was the area one would have to go through to reach Lost Izalith.

title: Cromwell the Pardoner
snippet:
Cromwell the Pardoner -  Dark Souls II - character - character_information 
 character_information : Cromwell, as his title implies, can be visited so the players may have their sins forgiven. This will remove the current sin title the player has, but it does allow hostile NPCs that the player provoked to become friendly again (the Royal Soldiers found in the Giant's Memories are excluded from this), as well as removing the damage penalty on the Lost Sinner's Sword, and thus reverting it to the normal damage it dealt.

He also sells many useful items, such as useful miracles (such as Great Heal and Perseverance) and the statusbite rings, which can greatly aid the player along the way.

He dons the Judgment Set, similarly to how Oswald of Carim donned the Black Set, and wields a Great Scythe.

title: Dark Set
snippet: Two of its drawbacks are that, to acquire it, the player must reach level +2 in the Darkwraith covenant, which can be both difficult and time-consuming, and the player must acquire Twinkling Titanite to upgrade it. Later in the game, however, the second issue can be nullified by being able to purchase the Twinkling Titanite from the Giant Blacksmith in Anor Londo for 8,000 souls per piece and by unlocking good Twinkling Titanite farming locations, such as Ash Lake or the Crystal Cave's boss area.

title: Mound-makers
snippet:
Mound-makers -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : The Mound-makers can be joined in the Undead Settlement. By navigating to a hidden area patrolled by numerous Thralls, the player can discover a non-hostile Hollow Manservant carrying an empty cage on its back. By examining the hollow, the player will enter the cage and be transported to the Pit of Hollows, below the Curse-rotted Greatwood's boss arena. This Manservant will be hostile if the Greatwood has been confronted or defeated, and thus cannot be interacted with.

Once there, the player must talk to Holy Knight Hodrick, who stands next to the covenant's Sacrificial Altar and who will give them the Mound-makers covenant item. If talked to again, he will give the player a Homeward Bone, which is required to leave the area without using the Darksign or committing suicide.

title: Sniper Crossbow (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Sniper Crossbow (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - availability 
 availability : Found in Lothric Castle, on a corpse on a small tower guarded by a Hollow Soldier that throws Undead Hunter Charms, before reaching the Dragon Barracks bonfire. To reach it, the player must drop into the moat before the Lothric Wyverns and follow the path to the right, defeating several Hollow Assassins and a Winged Knight in order to reach it.

title: Bonfire (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
:Alternatively, if the player entered by the Demon Ruins side, the bonfire can also be reached by traveling through the complex of tunnels below that conform the rest of the area.

***Demon Ruins**
:From the Abandoned Tomb, follow the tunnel down to reach the Smouldering Lake. Head toward the opposite side of the lake whilst hugging the left wall. To the right of the staircase that leads to the Old Demon King, look for an inclined path that goes upward. Follow it to reach a tunnel where the bonfire is found.

***Old Demon King**
:From the Abandoned Tomb, follow the tunnel down to reach the Smouldering Lake. A large fog door will be visible in the distance, beyond from where the Carthus Sand Worm attacks. Enter the mist into an optional boss arena, where one must face the Old Demon King; the bonfire will appear once the boss has been defeated.

title: Gyrm Great Hammer
snippet:
Gyrm Great Hammer -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Gyrm Great Hammer is a strong great hammer. Compared to the Dragon Tooth that has the same weight, it has the same attack rating, but much shorter range and does not have the unique bonus defense. In fact, it is the shortest great hammer in the game.

What makes this great hammer useful is it's moveset, which helps dealing more Poise damage than many other great hammer.

title: Covenant of Artorias
snippet:
Covenant of Artorias -  Dark Souls - ring - general_information 
 general_information : Covenant of Artorias allows the player to reach the Abyss. As such, it is necessary in order to reach the Four Kings boss battle. Without wearing the ring, it is impossible to survive the fall into the Abyss. Taking off the ring during the fight with the Four Kings will cause the player to be devoured by the Abyss. Other than this, the ring has no other purpose.

The Covenant of Artorias is one of the very few rings that do not carry over to NG+; players are required to kill Great Grey Wolf Sif every playthrough to obtain the ring and beat the game. This ring, when dropped, will end up in the chest behind Kingseeker Frampt after the player has quit and reloaded the game. However, in the remaster, it will automatically be in the player’s inventory.

title: Four Kings
snippet:
Using a ranged attack and staying at around 1-1.5 roll distance away in front of the king (just within the reach of his sword) makes him rely mostly on the vertical slashes and the occasional Homing Abyss Arrow or Life Drain. The Life Drain is also easier avoided since it looks less like Wrath of the Kings at this distance then it does close up, and the player already has a head start on getting out of reach.
Their homing attacks can be deflected by using Force or Wrath of the Gods, although it is safer to avoid the attacks entirely. Due to the speed at which the King approaches, the player will become vulnerable to other attacks during the casting animation. Deflecting the large homing shot will likely be fatal, since the duration of the attack lasts a fair while and doesn't collide with anything other than the player.
